subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU choice & unit-econ pathway
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexa.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:03:00Z
Subject: Prod inference capacity - initial numbers + budget

Kim, Marcus, Neha —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. A few follow-ups from our side as we start internal budgeting:

- Expected steady-state traffic: ~200M tokens/day (spiky between 120M - 350M).
- Peak concurrency goal: p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts (~50-150 tokens).
- Target go-live: mid-Jan 2027 (we'll have a small pilot in Dec).
- Procurement budget range for infra + managed service: $40k - $70k/month depending on SLA and performance.

Specific asks:
1) Ballpark cost per 1M tokens for a Dedicated reserved stack (H100 vs A100 options).
2) Recommended reserved capacity size to meet the above throughput and latency targets (initial + ramp path).
3) Any SKU or procurement docs you can share to speed PO.

Attaching a short usage snapshot (internal forecast). Happy to hop on a quick call — but a 1-pager with numbers would be perfect.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of AI Platform
Finexa
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexa.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Prod inference capacity - initial numbers + budget

Thanks Alicia — good context. Recap + a couple clarifying Qs below so we can baseline estimates.

Recap of your asks:
- Steady-state ~200M tokens/day (~6B/month). Peaks up to ~350M/day.
- p95 latency target ~250ms for shorter prompts.
- Budget window $40k-$70k/mo for infra + managed Redwood Dedicated.

Clarifying Qs (two quick ones):
- What fraction of tokens are generative (long responses) vs short reranks/embeddings? Rough split helps sizing KV cache + batch profiles.
- Are you aiming for a single-region setup (us-east) or multi-region active-active? That will affect reserved capacity sizing and cost.

Prelim ballpark unit-econ (rounded):
- H100 reserved pool (4 x H100 setup, optimized for low-latency): est. monthly platform+infra cost = $46,800 -> with 6B tokens/month -> ~ $7.8 per 1M tokens.
- A100 80GB reserved pool (8 x A100): est. monthly cost = $38,400 -> with 6B tokens/month -> ~ $6.4 per 1M tokens.

Notes on the numbers above:
- H100 configuration assumes smaller batch sizes and KV cache enabled to hit 250ms p95; better for tighter latency but higher infra cost.
- A100 option is more cost-efficient for throughput but may need modest increase in batch tuning and slightly higher p95.
- Both include Redwood Dedicated service (runtime, orchestration, monitoring) and expected autoscale buffers for short spikes.

Recommended ramp path (one pager):
1) Pilot (Dec): 1-2 reserved GPUs (A100) + hosted fallback. Validate token distribution and latency on real workload.
2) Prod initial (Jan): 4x H100 reserved (if latency-critical) or 8x A100 if budget-constrained; make this a 6-month commit to get better pricing.
3) Scale (post-3mo): Re-evaluate based on actual token per-second and KV cache hit rates; convert to banded reserve if needed.

I'll attach a quick SKU/estimate workbook and SOC2 snapshot. Marcus, Rishi — can you add any throughput assumptions I missed?

Next steps:
- Alicia: confirm token split (gen vs short) and single-region vs multi-region by EOD 11/05 if possible.
- Redwood: we'll follow up with a formal SKU estimate and a short SOW draft.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexa.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Prod inference capacity - initial numbers + budget

Quick throughput note from infra/benchmarking perspective — Alicia, thanks for the forecast. A couple practical items that will materially change the reserve sizing: 

- Average response length when generative: you listed variance — if mean is ~180 tokens, that implies roughly 200M * 180 = 36B tokens consumed by generative responses/month (this is higher than your blended 6B figure if the 200M/day was requests). Please confirm whether the 200M tokens/day is tokens returned by the model or user-input tokens.
- If the 200M/day number is actually total tokens (input+output), we can keep the 6B/month baseline. If it's response-only, monthly tokens could be 36B and drive materially different unit-econ.

Prelim revised capacity examples (to hit p95 <250ms assuming US-east, sustained):
- Latency-focused: 4x H100 (reserved) + 1x hot spare (for short spikes); est monthly cost: $46.8k. Effective tokens/month baseline 6B -> $/1M = $7.8. If tokens are 36B -> $/1M = $1.3.
- Cost-focused: 8x A100 (reserved); est monthly cost: $38.4k. Effective tokens/month baseline 6B -> $/1M = $6.4. If tokens are 36B -> $/1M = $1.07.

Why the big per-1M swing when tokens increase? Because fixed infra cost amortizes over more tokens; we assume throughput can scale with batching and caching. We'll include sensitivity rows in the workbook for 6B, 18B, 36B monthly token scenarios.

Attachments: capacity_sku_estimate_v2.xlsx (contains the sensitivity).

Action: Alicia — can you confirm whether your 200M/day is request-count or token-count? That single clarifier will let us finalize a recommended SKU and monthly number to put in a PO-ready estimate.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead Infrastructure Solutions, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Prod inference capacity - initial numbers + budget

Thanks team — quick clarifications per Marcus' note: the 200M/day figure I quoted is total tokens (input + output) averaged; generative output is roughly 60% of that. So monthly blended baseline is ~6B tokens.

We reviewed your numbers internally and prefer the H100 path to meet latency SLOs. Procurement asks:
- Please send a 6-month SOW and an itemized SKU estimate (we prefer line items for reserved GPUs, managed service fee, support SLA).
- We typically do monthly billing but can discuss a 12-month prepay if you offer uplift discounts.
- PO contact: procurement@finexa.com (cc'd).

Requested next steps:
1) Redwood: send SOW + PO-ready SKU spreadsheet (final numbers, payment terms) by 11/12.
2) Finexa: we'll prepare standard procurement paperwork and share PO within a week of SOW sign-off.

A couple final asks — can you include the SOC2 snapshot (redacted) and a short note on data residency for logs? I'm attaching our internal forecast and SOC checklist.

Thanks,
